cells.title: Memory Body Text 1
cells.description: The Bebe Miller Company works with memory as a resource for improvisation in performance. One way they do this is through a state they have devised called Redux. In a Redux, they actively work to recall a piece of set choreography they have performed in the past and reference aspects of it in the new performance.

additional_fields.text-content: The Bebe Miller Company works with memory as a resource for improvisation in performance. One way they do this is through a state they have devised called Redux. In a Redux, they actively work to recall a piece of set choreography they have performed in the past and reference aspects of it in the new performance.

cells.title: Memory CallOut Text 1
cells.description:
“We are actively mining the history that is in the present, looking to interrupt and further what we’ve set in motion over 15 years of working together.”
----- Bebe Miller

additional_fields.html-content:
“We are actively mining the history that is in the present, looking to interrupt and further what we’ve set in motion over 15 years of working together.”
----- Bebe Miller

cells.title: Memory CallOut Text 2
cells.description:
“There is an aspect of improvisation that asks you to shuffle through the various layers of right now in order to respond directly to the situation. We as a company have invested many years in researching this relationship between memory and the dynamics of body/mind/place/time. Redux is one example of this.”
----- Bebe Miller

additional_fields.html-content:
“There is an aspect of improvisation that asks you to shuffle through the various layers of right now in order to respond directly to the situation. We as a company have invested many years in researching this relationship between memory and the dynamics of body/mind/place/time. Redux is one example of this.”
----- Bebe Miller

cells.title: Memory Body Text 2
cells.description:
The Redux structure for improvisation is a way of consciously accessing embodied history or memory by recalling a set dance performed in the past and referencing it to create a new one. This creative process involves several strategies, including:

1. Quoting and resequencing choreographed actions

2. Transposing an action in time, space, shape, body part

3. Changing roles

4. Recalling the choreographed timing and sequence but not exact actions

5. Offering beginnings or endings of actions, waiting, and finding new solutions

6. Echoing the quality of touch from the past in a new action

cells.title: Memory CallOut Text 3
cells.description:
“We are calling on and opening up to things firing in deep embodied memory. Maybe it is a neurological unconscious score. We say yes to imagining the physical manifestation. We flow and then catch a remembered action before it completes and glides into something that's interesting at that time. Memory is always a fiction, the more we do it the more we remember the remembering.”
----- Angie Hauser

----- Angie Hauser

cells.title: Memory CallOut Text 4
cells.description:
"Redux is a choreographic improvisation structure based on recall of existing material. The interplay between what’s remembered, what’s recalled, and what’s new is the basis of Redux.”
----- Bebe Miller

additional_fields.html-content:
"Redux is a choreographic improvisation structure based on recall of existing material. The interplay between what’s remembered, what’s recalled, and what’s new is the basis of Redux.”
----- Bebe Miller

cells.title: Memory CallOut Text 5
cells.description:
“We have recognized that the power of the choreographed moment has much to do with the live intentions that are set on various vectors, and with improvisation we are interested in how we (and an audience) might respond to that reality. We are arriving at the level of exquisite detail in repeated actions—but making them new each time.”
----- Bebe Miller
